facts.fact: NIDA's Director General says the authentication layer for the new digital ID, known as AMBAS, is at the contracting stage.

RWA.note: Civil registry mentioned only for name changes.

facts.fact: NIDA's Director General says the digital ID complies with Rwanda's personal data protection and privacy law, requiring user consent before data access.
facts.system: personal data protection and privacy law

facts.fact: NIDA's Director General says over 300,000 people had registered for the new digital ID by 20 November 2025, in a population the article's link says passes 13 million.
NIDA's Director General says the new digital ID will be issued from birth, unlike the current ID which starts at 16, with residents receiving an SDID number once the core system is live.

RWA.note: Nothing on who operates or owns the system.
No register keyed on the ID stated.

facts.fact: NIDA's Director General says the core digital identity system is under procurement, biometric enrolment is under way in Huye, Gisagara and Nyanza districts and nationwide data collection is to conclude by June 2026.

RWA.note: No other system checking against the ID is in service or contracted.

facts.fact: NIDA's Director General says the new digital ID will include groups previously left out, such as asylum seekers and stateless persons in border areas.

RWA.note: Nothing on local civil registration offices.
